vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is in the DividendPayingToken contract. The distributeDividends(uint256 amount) function is public with no access control, allowing anyone to call it and artificially inflate the magnifiedDividendPerShare value. This affects dividend calculations for all token holders. When combined with the ability to become a token holder, an attacker can inflate dividends and then withdraw more dividend tokens than they contributed. The setDividendTokenAddress function also has a weak authorization check (tx.origin == hardcoded address), but the main issue is the unauthorized distributeDividends function.
attack_strategy: 1. Acquire DCAKE tokens to become a token holder in the dividend tracker. 2. Send some dividend tokens (CAKE) to the dividend tracker contract. 3. Call distributeDividends on the tracker with a large amount to inflate the dividend per share. 4. Withdraw dividends, receiving more CAKE tokens than we sent to the tracker. The key is that distributeDividends only updates accounting, not token balances, so we can inflate the perceived dividends distributed.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get DCAKE tokens by buying from the Uniswap pair. 2. Get CAKE tokens (dividend token) using deal(). 3. Send a small amount of CAKE to the cakeDividendTracker. 4. Call distributeDividends on cakeDividendTracker with a much larger amount (e.g., 100x what we sent). 5. Call claim() on DogeCake contract to withdraw inflated dividends. 6. Verify CAKE balance increased more than what we sent to the tracker.
